prompt: A phone costs $\$600$ new. It loses $25\%$ of its value every year. What is it worth after $2$ years, in dollars?
hint: Losing $25\%$ means keeping $75\%$. Turn that into a decay factor and use it once per year.

hints.text: Losing $25\%$ means keeping $75\%$. Turn that into a decay factor and use it once per year.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: a $\$100$ item that loses $50\%$ a year is worth $\$50$ after one year and $\$25$ after two. Same move — multiply by the keep-factor once per year.
The factor is $100\% - 25\% = 75\% = 0.75$. After year 1 the phone is worth $600 \times 0.75 = 450$. Apply the factor to $450$ once more.
Year 2 gives $450 \times 0.75 = 337.5$, so the phone is worth $337.50$ dollars.

explanation: Losing $25\%$ each year means $75\%$ of the value stays, so the decay factor is $0.75$.
After the first year the value is $600 \times 0.75 = 450$ dollars.
The second year shrinks that new value: $450 \times 0.75 = 337.5$, so the phone is worth $337.50$ dollars.

alternativeExplanations.title: Subtract a quarter each year
steps: Losing $25\%$ is losing a quarter, and a quarter of $600$ is $150$, so year one ends at $600 - 150 = 450$ dollars.
The second loss is a quarter of the NEW value: a quarter of $450$ is $112.5$ dollars.
Subtracting gives $450 - 112.5 = 337.5$, so the phone is worth $337.5$ dollars after two years.

alternativeExplanations.title: One power instead of two steps
steps: Each year keeps $75\%$ of the value, so two years multiply by $0.75$ twice, which is $0.75^2$.
Work out the combined factor first: $0.75 \times 0.75 = 0.5625$.
Apply that single factor to the starting price: $600 \times 0.5625 = 337.5$ dollars.
